Trying to prove α = log₂(3/2) is irrational and want to know whether mathlib already has it (or a close-enough lemma) before writing a proof. The elementary argument: if 2^p = (3/2)^q then 2^(p+q) = 3^q, so FTA forces p + q = q = 0.

import Mathlib
open Real

theorem log_three_halves_irrational :
    Irrational (Real.logb 2 (3/2)) := by
  sorry

Two questions:

  1. Is there an existing lemma , Irrational.logb, Nat.log_irrational, or similar , that gives this directly under a coprime-base/argument hypothesis? Couldn't find one searching Irrational + log.

  2. If not, is Real.logb 2 (3/2) the idiomatic statement, or would mathlib prefer the ratio form Real.log 3 / Real.log 2 ∉ Set.range ((↑) : ℚ → ℝ), or 12 * Real.log 3 ≠ 19 * Real.log 2?

Thanks. Three candidate statements at increasing generality, in case any are upstream-worthy:

import Mathlib
open Real

/-- Distinct primes case. -/
theorem Nat.Prime.irrational_logb {p q : ℕ}
    (hp : p.Prime) (hq : q.Prime) (hpq : p ≠ q) :
    Irrational (Real.logb p q) := by
  sorry

/-- Coprime integers ≥ 2 case. Subsumes the prime case. -/
theorem Nat.Coprime.irrational_logb {p q : ℕ}
    (hp : 1 < p) (hq : 1 < q) (h : p.Coprime q) :
    Irrational (Real.logb p q) := by
  sorry

/-- Multiplicative-independence case. Subsumes both above:
`Real.logb p q` is irrational iff `p, q ≥ 2` are not both
powers of a common natural number `n ≥ 2`. -/
theorem Real.irrational_logb_of_not_pow_pow {p q : ℕ}
    (hp : 1 < p) (hq : 1 < q)
    (h : ∀ (n a b : ℕ), 1 < n → 0 < a → 0 < b → ¬(p = n ^ a ∧ q = n ^ b)) :
    Irrational (Real.logb p q) := by
  sorry

For my application I need Irrational (Real.logb 2 (3/2)), which I'd derive from the coprime case via Real.logb 2 (3/2) = Real.logb 2 3 - 1 and Irrational.sub_int. Happy to PR whichever level you think is the right target — my instinct is the coprime case as the named lemma with the prime case as a corollary, and the multiplicative-independence case deferred. Open to a different naming convention; I picked Nat.Coprime.irrational_logb to mirror existing Nat.Coprime.* API.

Irrational (logb b x) ↔, and Irrational (logb 2 3)

import Mathlib

theorem Real.irrational_logb_nat_nat_iff {b x : ℕ} :
    Irrational (logb b x) ↔ 1 < b ∧ 1 < x ∧ (∀ kb kx, b ^ kb = x ^ kx → kx = 0) := by
  refine ⟨fun hirr ↦ ?_, fun ⟨hb, hx, h⟩ ↦ ?_⟩
  · have hb : 1 < b := not_not.mp fun h ↦ hirr <|
      by cases Nat.le_one_iff_eq_zero_or_eq_one.mp <| Nat.le_of_not_lt h <;> simp [*]
    have hx : 1 < x := not_not.mp fun h ↦ hirr <|
      by cases Nat.le_one_iff_eq_zero_or_eq_one.mp <| Nat.le_of_not_lt h <;> simp [*]
    refine ⟨hb, hx, fun kb kx h ↦ not_not.mp fun hkx ↦ hirr ?_⟩
    suffices logb b x = (kb / kx : ℚ) by grind
    apply logb_eq_iff_rpow_eq (zero_lt_one.trans <| Nat.one_lt_cast.mpr hb)
      (ne_of_gt <| Nat.one_lt_cast.mpr hb) (zero_lt_one.trans <| Nat.one_lt_cast.mpr hx) |>.mpr
    apply_fun (fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ (1 / kx : ℝ)) at h
    push_cast at h
    simp only [hkx, one_div, Nat.cast_nonneg, ← rpow_natCast_mul, ne_eq, Nat.cast_eq_zero, rpow_one,
      not_false_eq_true, mul_inv_cancel₀] at h
    convert h
    push_cast
    grind
  have h_pow := by apply @rpow_logb b x <;> norm_cast <;> lia
  have h_pos := by apply @logb_pos b x <;> norm_cast
  refine fun ⟨q, hq⟩ ↦ q.den_nz <| h q.num.toNat q.den ?_
  rw [← hq, ← q.num_div_den, Rat.cast_div, Rat.cast_natCast] at h_pow
  apply_fun (· ^ q.den) at h_pow
  have numpos := Rat.num_pos.mpr <| Rat.cast_pos.mp <| hq ▸ h_pos
  rw [← rpow_mul_natCast <| by positivity, div_mul_cancel₀ _ <| Nat.cast_ne_zero.mpr q.den_ne_zero,
    Rat.cast_intCast, ← @Int.toNat_of_nonneg q.num numpos.le] at h_pow
  norm_cast at h_pow

theorem irrational_logb_two_three : Irrational (Real.logb 2 3) := by
  refine Real.irrational_logb_nat_nat_iff.mpr ⟨by norm_num, by norm_num, fun kb kx h ↦ ?_⟩
  apply_fun (·.factorization 3) at h
  rw [Nat.Prime.factorization_pow Nat.prime_two, Nat.Prime.factorization_pow Nat.prime_three] at h
  simp only [ne_eq, Nat.succ_ne_self, not_false_eq_true, Finsupp.single_eq_of_ne,
    Finsupp.single_eq_same] at h
  rw [h]

My goal is Decidable <| Irrational (logb b x) for any b x : ℚ

for my use case it'd be a one-liner via decide once it lands.

And for the general Irrational (logb b x) iff for naturals, I wanted to also have these alternative assumptions (not all of them are iff):

  • ∀ kb kx, b ^ kb = x ^ kx → kb = 0
  • ∀ kb kx, b ^ kb = x ^ kx → kx = 0
  • ¬∃ n kb kx, b = n ^ kb ∧ x = n ^ kx
  • Nat.Coprime b x
  • b.gcd x < b.min x
  • constant (p ↦ padicValNat p b / gcd (padicValNat p b) (padicValNat p x)) ∧ constant (p ↦ padicValNat p x / gcd (padicValNat p b) (padicValNat p x)) (the "constant" is made up, but basically I mean that the function is constant)

I noted that these might be useful as they relate to the pow equals pow condition, most of them from #28557:

  • docs#pow_eq_pow_iff_of_coprime
  • docs#Nat.exists_eq_pow_of_pow_eq_pow
  • docs#Nat.exists_eq_pow_of_exponent_coprime_of_pow_eq_pow
  • docs#Nat.exponent_eq_exponent_mul_factorization_of_prime_pow_eq_base_pow
  • docs#Nat.exponent_dvd_of_prime_pow_eq_pow
  • docs#Nat.exists_base_eq_prime_pow_of_prime_pow_eq_base_pow

And finally, since I wanted to get Decidable I mostly wanted to show an iff with the last condition I listed, that uses the prime factorization. So I played around with Nat.factorization and found out that Finsupp.zipWith is noncomputable sadly:

import Mathlib
example (b x : ℕ) : True := by
  let facGCD := Finsupp.zipWith Nat.gcd (by rfl) b.factorization x.factorization
  let facB := Finsupp.zipWith (· / ·) (by rfl) b.factorization facGCD
  let facX := Finsupp.zipWith (· / ·) (by rfl) x.factorization facGCD
  let supp := ∃ k, Set.EqOn facB.toFun (Function.const _ k) (b.primeFactors ∪ x.primeFactors)
  sorry

(since then I found out I could use b.factorization.toDFinsupp to get computability for Decidable)
